title: Cohomological correspondence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be
separated of finite type
over $k$. A *cohomological correspondence* consists of a
separated finite-type
scheme $C$ with a morphism

$$
c=(c_1,c_2):C\longrightarrow X\times_sX,
$$

and, for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, a morphism

$$
u:Lc_2^*K\longrightarrow Rc_1^!K
$$

in $D(C,A)$, where $Lc_2^*$ is the
derived pullback and
$Rc_1^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
of [def-trf-admissibility]; $c_2$ is the ordinary pullback leg
and $c_1$ the exceptional leg. The correspondence is
*admissible* if $c_1$ and every base change of $c_1$ occurring
below are exceptionally admissible at $A$.

Its statement matches the current blueprint main-20261015 sec-six-functors-basics/sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation/def-trf-correspondence.md (order 2430) character for character; the old master copy (order 2086) differs only in its order number and the 'recorded in advance' note. I opened all six cited dependencies; each exists, is split and reviewed, and none is merged. C and X are separated finite-type k-schemes, so c1 is a separated finite-type k-morphism between finite-type k-schemes. That is exactly the setting where def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image constructs Rc1^! and def-trf-admissibility defines admissibility. Lc2^* is the derived pullback of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, which applies because ell is not p. So u lives in D(C_proet,A) with A=A_{E,n} and n>=1, and K is in the pro-etale category D^b_ctf. No other coefficient category is substituted. The admissibility predicate is the fixed-stage notion; its base-change exchange is Rg'_*Rf'^! -> Rf^!Rg_*, and I checked that this direction is correct. The item only names the predicate and claims no exchange of its own. I tested the small cases: K=0; X=C=Spec k with both legs the identity, where u is any endomorphism; empty C; and empty X. There is no dependency cycle (12010 nodes walked). def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs generalizes this item but cites it, and sk-d-corr is a different ambient notion, so same_as=[] is correct.
